mechanism: "avoidpartialspends" is a DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS row (src/config-options.lisp:436) with no reader anywhere in src/. The WCC struct (Core's CCoinControl, src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:261-282) declares AVOID-PARTIAL-SPENDS with no initform, so a fresh coin control starts NIL, and there are exactly two writers in the tree: the -maxapsfee retry copy at :2388-2390 and the avoid_reuse OR at :3129-3131. Core has the same two raisers -- wallet/spend.cpp:1466-1478 for the retry and wallet/rpc/spend.cpp:313 (m_avoid_partial_spends |= m_avoid_address_reuse) -- plus the one we lack: every CCoinControl constructor runs m_avoid_partial_spends = gArgs.GetBoolArg("-avoidpartialspends", DEFAULT_AVOIDPARTIALSPENDS) (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/coincontrol.cpp:9-13), so the option is the starting value for every spend the wallet builds and the other two can only raise it. Everything downstream is present and correct on our side: CSEL-PARAMS-AVOID-PARTIAL-SPENDS is set from the coin control at :1939, %GROUP-OUTPUTS branches on it at :809 the way Core's GroupOutputs does, the >OUTPUT_GROUP_MAX_ENTRIES shuffle is at :1381 (Core spend.cpp:889-891), and -maxapsfee is a real implemented option (*wallet-max-aps-fee*, default 0 = Core's DEFAULT_MAX_AVOIDPARTIALSPEND_FEE). The option's own switch is the only missing piece.
consequence: An operator who set avoidpartialspends=1 expects every spend from a reused address to sweep that address's outputs together; instead coins are selected per output, leaving the remainder behind to be linked to the next spend through the shared address -- the linkage the option is documented to remove. Funds are unaffected and no transaction is made invalid. Bounded more tightly than the title suggests, which is why this stays S3 rather than being raised on the address-linking test: (1) Core's own default is false, so our behaviour equals Core's DEFAULT behaviour and only an explicit opt-in diverges; (2) the option is therefore always supplied and the startup WARN names it (measured); (3) the -maxapsfee retry still applies grouping opportunistically whenever it costs no more than *wallet-max-aps-fee* extra satoshis, so the common case where grouping is free already groups, and what is lost is grouping that would cost more; and (4) the avoid_reuse wallet flag still forces it unconditionally. What an operator cannot do today is make grouping unconditional regardless of fee, which is precisely what the option means.

fix_shape: Reproduce Core's constructor default rather than patching the call sites. Promote "avoidpartialspends" to a real DEFINE-OPTION boolean (default false, Core's DEFAULT_AVOIDPARTIALSPENDS), bind it to a wallet special next to the existing *wallet-max-aps-fee* -- which is already wired the same way and is set through src/node/rpc-config.lisp:69 -- and make it the INITFORM of the WCC struct's AVOID-PARTIAL-SPENDS slot, so every coin control built anywhere starts from it exactly as CCoinControl's constructor does. That leaves the two existing writers untouched and correct: the avoid_reuse OR at :3129-3131 can still only raise it, and the -maxapsfee retry at :2385-2390 is already guarded by (not (wcc-avoid-partial-spends cc)) so it correctly stops running the ungrouped attempt once the option is on -- which is the behaviour the operator asked for, grouping regardless of the extra fee. Note the slot has no initform today, so this is a defstruct change and needs cl-workbench validation run cold-unit-fresh. A test should build a spend from several outputs at one address with the special NIL and with it T and assert the input set is one output versus the whole address, with the per-call avoid_reuse path as the positive control.
